newsitem.title: USA: Missouri soybean harvest lags from a year ago.
newsitem.headline: Missouri soybean harvest lags from a year ago.

text.p: Missouri's soybean crop was 60 percent harvested, about five days behind last year's 76 percent and four days behind the five-year average of 70 percent, the state's Agriculture Statistics Service said for the week ending Sunday.
Soybeans were rated 14 percent excellent, 52 good, 28 fair and six poor, similar to a week earlier.
Corn was 70 percent harvested, about two days ahead of last year's 67 percent and the same as the five-year average.
Virtually all of the crop has been harvested across the southern third of the state.
Sorghum was 97 percent mature, just slightly behind both last year's and the five-year average of 98 percent. Sixty-six percent of sorghum was harvested versus 72 a year ago and 73 on average.
Winter wheat was 65 percent planted and 42 percent emerged, versus 78 and 44 a year ago and the 68 and 43 averages.
Cotton was 69 percent harvested versus 77 a year ago and the 75 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated 18 percent surplus, 77 adequate and five percent short.
